Order 
This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 14.02.2019 passed by I Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur, Dist. Dhar (M.P.) in Claim Case No.175/2015, whereby an amount of Rs.74,000/- with interest has been awarded to the appellant/injured Arjun.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2 . Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the income of the appellant has not been properly assessed by the learned Claims Tribunal whereas as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, the income of an unskilled labour on the date of incident is Rs.4945/-.

sentences.text: He further submits that in the accident appellant / injured has suffered fracture in right leg tibia fibula and rod was inserted.

He further submits that looking to the age of the injured 25 years on the date of incident, 40% of income should have been added in the head of future prospects.
He further submits that a meager amount has been awarded in the head of pain and suffering and no amount has been awarded in the head of conveyance.
On these submissions, he prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.

Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.
From perusal of the record, it reveals that in the accident the appellant has suffered grievous injuries and fracture in right leg tibia fibula and rod was inserted.
Ex. P/9
has been produced to establish the permanent disability of appellant and Dr. Mahesh Borasi has also proved the disability certificate
, therefore, keeping in view the evidence available in this regard, this Court is of the view that at least 12% permanent disability should have been assessed.

In light of the aforesaid, where the income of the injured is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8928 3 MA-3324-2019 taken on guess work, Circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act should be resorted to.

Accordingly,
on the date of accident i.e. on 30.12.2012, income of the appellant/injured is to be taken as Rs.4945/- considering him as 'Unskilled Labour' and for this judgment passed by the Apex Court in Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav , (2022) 1 SCC 198 shall be referred.

8. The appeal is valued as Rs. 1 Lakh and for the rest of the amount, the appellant/injured will pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days from today and only thereafter enhanced amount will be disbursed.
